- Updated bundled idna to 2.2.


## 2.12.5 (2017-01-18) [¶](https://docs.python-requests.org/en/latest/community/updates/\#id52 "Link to this heading")

**Bugfixes**

- Fixed an issue with JSON encoding detection, specifically detecting
big-endian UTF-32 with BOM.


## 2.12.4 (2016-12-14) [¶](https://docs.python-requests.org/en/latest/community/updates/\#id53 "Link to this heading")

**Bugfixes**

- Fixed regression from 2.12.2 where non-string types were rejected in
the basic auth parameters. While support for this behaviour has been
re-added, the behaviour is deprecated and will be removed in the
future.


## 2.12.3 (2016-12-01) [¶](https://docs.python-requests.org/en/latest/community/updates/\#id54 "Link to this heading")

**Bugfixes**

- Fixed regression from v2.12.1 for URLs with schemes that begin with
“http”. These URLs have historically been processed as though they
were HTTP-schemed URLs, and so have had parameters added. This was
removed in v2.12.2 in an overzealous attempt to resolve problems
with IDNA-encoding those URLs. This change was reverted: the other
fixes for IDNA-encoding have been judged to be sufficient to return
to the behaviour Requests had before v2.12.0.


## 2.12.2 (2016-11-30) [¶](https://docs.python-requests.org/en/latest/community/updates/\#id55 "Link to this heading")

**Bugfixes**

- Fixed several issues with IDNA-encoding URLs that are technically
invalid but which are widely accepted. Requests will now attempt to
IDNA-encode a URL if it can but, if it fails, and the host contains
only ASCII characters, it will be passed through optimistically.
This will allow users to opt-in to using IDNA2003 themselves if they
want to, and will also allow technically invalid but still common
hostnames.

- Fixed an issue where URLs with leading whitespace would raise
InvalidSchema errors.

- Fixed an issue where some URLs without the HTTP or HTTPS schemes
would still have HTTP URL preparation applied to them.

- Fixed an issue where Unicode strings could not be used in basic
auth.

- Fixed an issue encountered by some Requests plugins where
constructing a Response object would cause Response.content to
raise an AttributeError.


## 2.12.1 (2016-11-16) [¶](https://docs.python-requests.org/en/latest/community/updates/\#id56 "Link to this heading")

**Bugfixes**

- Updated setuptools ‘security’ extra for the new PyOpenSSL backend in
urllib3.


**Miscellaneous**

- Updated bundled urllib3 to 1.19.1.


## 2.12.0 (2016-11-15) [¶](https://docs.python-requests.org/en/latest/community/updates/\#id57 "Link to this heading")

**Improvements**

- Updated support for internationalized domain names from IDNA2003 to
IDNA2008. This updated support is required for several forms of IDNs
and is mandatory for .de domains.

- Much improved heuristics for guessing content lengths: Requests will
no longer read an entire StringIO into memory.

- Much improved logic for recalculating Content-Length headers for
PreparedRequest objects.

- Improved tolerance for file-like objects that have no tell method
but do have a seek method.

- Anything that is a subclass of Mapping is now treated like a
dictionary by the data= keyword argument.

- Requests now tolerates empty passwords in proxy credentials, rather
than stripping the credentials.

- If a request is made with a file-like object as the body and that
request is redirected with a 307 or 308 status code, Requests will
now attempt to rewind the body object so it can be replayed.


**Bugfixes**

- When calling response.close, the call to close will be
propagated through to non-urllib3 backends.

- Fixed issue where the ALL\_PROXY environment variable would be
preferred over scheme-specific variables like HTTP\_PROXY.

- Fixed issue where non-UTF8 reason phrases got severely mangled by
falling back to decoding using ISO 8859-1 instead.

- Fixed a bug where Requests would not correctly correlate cookies set
when using custom Host headers if those Host headers did not use the
native string type for the platform.


**Miscellaneous**

- Updated bundled urllib3 to 1.19.

- Updated bundled certifi certs to 2016.09.26.


## 2.11.1 (2016-08-17) [¶](https://docs.python-requests.org/en/latest/community/updates/\#id58 "Link to this heading")

**Bugfixes**

- Fixed a bug when using iter\_content with decode\_unicode=True for
streamed bodies would raise AttributeError. This bug was
introduced in 2.11.

- Strip Content-Type and Transfer-Encoding headers from the header
block when following a redirect that transforms the verb from
POST/PUT to GET.


## 2.11.0 (2016-08-08) [¶](https://docs.python-requests.org/en/latest/community/updates/\#id59 "Link to this heading")

**Improvements**

- Added support for the ALL\_PROXY environment variable.

- Reject header values that contain leading whitespace or newline
characters to reduce risk of header smuggling.


**Bugfixes**

- Fixed occasional TypeError when attempting to decode a JSON
response that occurred in an error case. Now correctly returns a
ValueError.

- Requests would incorrectly ignore a non-CIDR IP address in the
NO\_PROXY environment variables: Requests now treats it as a
specific IP.

- Fixed a bug when sending JSON data that could cause us to encounter
obscure OpenSSL errors in certain network conditions (yes, really).

- Added type checks to ensure that iter\_content only accepts
integers and None for chunk sizes.

- Fixed issue where responses whose body had not been fully consumed
would have the underlying connection closed but not returned to the
connection pool, which could cause Requests to hang in situations
where the HTTPAdapter had been configured to use a blocking
connection pool.


**Miscellaneous**

- Updated bundled urllib3 to 1.16.

- Some previous releases accidentally accepted non-strings as
acceptable header values. This release does not.


## 2.10.0 (2016-04-29) [¶](https://docs.python-requests.org/en/latest/community/updates/\#id60 "Link to this heading")

**New Features**

- SOCKS Proxy Support! (requires PySocks;
$ pip install requests\[socks\])


**Miscellaneous**

- Updated bundled urllib3 to 1.15.1.


## 2.9.2 (2016-04-29) [¶](https://docs.python-requests.org/en/latest/community/updates/\#id61 "Link to this heading")

**Improvements**

- Change built-in CaseInsensitiveDict (used for headers) to use
OrderedDict as its underlying datastore.


**Bugfixes**

- Don’t use redirect\_cache if allow\_redirects=False

- When passed objects that throw exceptions from tell(), send them
via chunked transfer encoding instead of failing.

- Raise a ProxyError for proxy related connection issues.


## 2.9.1 (2015-12-21) [¶](https://docs.python-requests.org/en/latest/community/updates/\#id62 "Link to this heading")

**Bugfixes**

- Resolve regression introduced in 2.9.0 that made it impossible to
send binary strings as bodies in Python 3.

- Fixed errors when calculating cookie expiration dates in certain
locales.


**Miscellaneous**

- Updated bundled urllib3 to 1.13.1.


## 2.9.0 (2015-12-15) [¶](https://docs.python-requests.org/en/latest/community/updates/\#id63 "Link to this heading")

**Minor Improvements** (Backwards compatible)

- The verify keyword argument now supports being passed a path to a
directory of CA certificates, not just a single-file bundle.

- Warnings are now emitted when sending files opened in text mode.

- Added the 511 Network Authentication Required status code to the
status code registry.


**Bugfixes**

- For file-like objects that are not sought to the very beginning, we
now send the content length for the number of bytes we will actually
read, rather than the total size of the file, allowing partial file
uploads.

- When uploading file-like objects, if they are empty or have no
obvious content length we set Transfer-Encoding: chunked rather
than Content-Length: 0.

- We correctly receive the response in buffered mode when uploading
chunked bodies.

- We now handle being passed a query string as a bytestring on Python
3, by decoding it as UTF-8.

- Sessions are now closed in all cases (exceptional and not) when
using the functional API rather than leaking and waiting for the
garbage collector to clean them up.

- Correctly handle digest auth headers with a malformed qop
directive that contains no token, by treating it the same as if no
qop directive was provided at all.

- Minor performance improvements when removing specific cookies by
name.


**Miscellaneous**

- Updated urllib3 to 1.13.


## 2.8.1 (2015-10-13) [¶](https://docs.python-requests.org/en/latest/community/updates/\#id64 "Link to this heading")

**Bugfixes**

- Update certificate bundle to match certifi 2015.9.6.2’s weak
certificate bundle.

- Fix a bug in 2.8.0 where requests would raise ConnectTimeout
instead of ConnectionError

- When using the PreparedRequest flow, requests will now correctly
respect the json parameter. Broken in 2.8.0.

- When using the PreparedRequest flow, requests will now correctly
handle a Unicode-string method name on Python 2. Broken in 2.8.0.


## 2.8.0 (2015-10-05) [¶](https://docs.python-requests.org/en/latest/community/updates/\#id65 "Link to this heading")

**Minor Improvements** (Backwards Compatible)

- Requests now supports per-host proxies. This allows the proxies
dictionary to have entries of the form
{‘<scheme>://<hostname>’: ‘<proxy>’}. Host-specific proxies will
be used in preference to the previously-supported scheme-specific
ones, but the previous syntax will continue to work.

- Response.raise\_for\_status now prints the URL that failed as part
of the exception message.

- requests.utils.get\_netrc\_auth now takes an raise\_errors kwarg,
defaulting to False. When True, errors parsing .netrc files
cause exceptions to be thrown.

- Change to bundled projects import logic to make it easier to
unbundle requests downstream.

- Changed the default User-Agent string to avoid leaking data on
Linux: now contains only the requests version.


**Bugfixes**

- The json parameter to post() and friends will now only be used
if neither data nor files are present, consistent with the
documentation.

- We now ignore empty fields in the NO\_PROXY environment variable.

- Fixed problem where httplib.BadStatusLine would get raised if
combining stream=True with contextlib.closing.

- Prevented bugs where we would attempt to return the same connection
back to the connection pool twice when sending a Chunked body.

- Miscellaneous minor internal changes.

- Digest Auth support is now thread safe.


**Updates**

**Bugfixes**

cookie without a host value set would use the hostname for the
redirected URL exposing requests users to session fixation attacks
and potentially cookie stealing. This was disclosed privately by
Matthew Daley of \[BugFuzz\]( [https://bugfuzz.com](https://bugfuzz.com/)). This affects all
versions of requests from v2.1.0 to v2.5.3 (inclusive on both ends).

## 2.4.0 (2014-08-29) [¶](https://docs.python-requests.org/en/latest/community/updates/\#id77 "Link to this heading")

## 2.3.0 (2014-05-16) [¶](https://docs.python-requests.org/en/latest/community/updates/\#id78 "Link to this heading")

**API Changes**

- New Response property is\_redirect, which is true when the
library could have processed this response as a redirection (whether
or not it actually did).

- The timeout parameter now affects requests with both stream=True
and stream=False equally.

- The change in v2.0.0 to mandate explicit proxy schemes has been
reverted. Proxy schemes now default to http://.

- The CaseInsensitiveDict used for HTTP headers now behaves like a
normal dictionary when references as string or viewed in the
interpreter.


**Bugfixes**

- No longer expose Authorization or Proxy-Authorization headers on
redirect. Fix CVE-2014-1829 and CVE-2014-1830 respectively.

- Authorization is re-evaluated each redirect.

- On redirect, pass url as native strings.

- Fall-back to autodetected encoding for JSON when Unicode detection
fails.

- Headers set to None on the Session are now correctly not sent.

- Correctly honor decode\_unicode even if it wasn’t used earlier in
the same response.

- Stop advertising compress as a supported Content-Encoding.

- The Response.history parameter is now always a list.

- Many, many urllib3 bugfixes.

**Bugfixes**

- Avoid many many exceptions from the buggy implementation of
proxy\_bypass on OS X in Python 2.6.

- Avoid crashing when attempting to get authentication credentials
from ~/.netrc when running as a user without a home directory.

- Use the correct pool size for pools of connections to proxies.

- Fix iteration of CookieJar objects.

- Ensure that cookies are persisted over redirect.

- Switch back to using chardet, since it has merged with charade.


## 2.1.0 (2013-12-05) [¶](https://docs.python-requests.org/en/latest/community/updates/\#id81 "Link to this heading")

- Updated CA Bundle, of course.

- Cookies set on individual Requests through a Session (e.g. via
Session.get()) are no longer persisted to the Session.

- Clean up connections when we hit problems during chunked upload,
rather than leaking them.

- Return connections to the pool when a chunked upload is successful,
rather than leaking it.

- Match the HTTPbis recommendation for HTTP 301 redirects.

- Prevent hanging when using streaming uploads and Digest Auth when a
401 is received.

- Values of headers set by Requests are now always the native string
type.

- Fix previously broken SNI support.

- Fix accessing HTTP proxies using proxy authentication.

- Unencode HTTP Basic usernames and passwords extracted from URLs.

- Support for IP address ranges for no\_proxy environment variable

- Parse headers correctly when users override the default Host:
header.

- Avoid munging the URL in case of case-sensitive servers.

- Looser URL handling for non-HTTP/HTTPS urls.

- Accept unicode methods in Python 2.6 and 2.7.

- More resilient cookie handling.

- Make Response objects pickleable.

- Actually added MD5-sess to Digest Auth instead of pretending to like
last time.

- Updated internal urllib3.

- Fixed @Lukasa’s lack of taste.


## 2.0.1 (2013-10-24) [¶](https://docs.python-requests.org/en/latest/community/updates/\#id82 "Link to this heading")

for the future

- Fixed: Correctly lowercase a redirect scheme.

## 2.0.0 (2013-09-24) [¶](https://docs.python-requests.org/en/latest/community/updates/\#id83 "Link to this heading")

**API Changes:**

- Keys in the Headers dictionary are now native strings on all Python
versions, i.e. bytestrings on Python 2, unicode on Python 3.

- Proxy URLs now _must_ have an explicit scheme. A MissingSchema
exception will be raised if they don’t.

- Timeouts now apply to read time if Stream=False.

- RequestException is now a subclass of IOError, not
RuntimeError.

- Added new method to PreparedRequest objects:
PreparedRequest.copy().

- Added new method to Session objects: Session.update\_request().
This method updates a Request object with the data (e.g. cookies)
stored on the Session.

- Added new method to Session objects: Session.prepare\_request().
This method updates and prepares a Request object, and returns the
corresponding PreparedRequest object.

- Added new method to HTTPAdapter objects:
HTTPAdapter.proxy\_headers(). This should not be called directly,
but improves the subclass interface.

- httplib.IncompleteRead exceptions caused by incorrect chunked
encoding will now raise a Requests ChunkedEncodingError instead.

- Invalid percent-escape sequences now cause a Requests InvalidURL
exception to be raised.

- HTTP 208 no longer uses reason phrase “im\_used”. Correctly uses
“already\_reported”.

- HTTP 226 reason added (“im\_used”).


**Bugfixes:**

- Vastly improved proxy support, including the CONNECT verb. Special
thanks to the many contributors who worked towards this improvement.

- Cookies are now properly managed when 401 authentication responses
are received.

- Chunked encoding fixes.

- Support for mixed case schemes.

- Better handling of streaming downloads.

- Retrieve environment proxies from more locations.

- Minor cookies fixes.

- Improved redirect behaviour.

- Improved streaming behaviour, particularly for compressed data.

- Miscellaneous small Python 3 text encoding bugs.

- .netrc no longer overrides explicit auth.

- Cookies set by hooks are now correctly persisted on Sessions.

- Fix problem with cookies that specify port numbers in their host
field.

- BytesIO can be used to perform streaming uploads.

- More generous parsing of the no\_proxy environment variable.

- Non-string objects can be passed in data values alongside files.

- Make Session objects picklable.

- ValueError for invalid schema URLs.


## 0.10.2 (2012-01-15) [¶](https://docs.python-requests.org/en/latest/community/updates/\#id117 "Link to this heading")

- Vastly improved URL quoting.

- Additional allowed cookie key values.

- Attempted fix for “Too many open files” Error

- Replace unicode errors on first pass, no need for second pass.

- Append ‘/’ to bare-domain urls before query insertion.

- Exceptions now inherit from RuntimeError.

- Binary uploads + auth fix.

- Bugfixes.


## 0.10.1 (2012-01-23) [¶](https://docs.python-requests.org/en/latest/community/updates/\#id118 "Link to this heading")

- PYTHON 3 SUPPORT!

- Dropped 2.5 Support. ( _Backwards Incompatible_)


## 0.10.0 (2012-01-21) [¶](https://docs.python-requests.org/en/latest/community/updates/\#id119 "Link to this heading")

- Response.content is now bytes-only. ( _Backwards Incompatible_)

- New Response.text is unicode-only.

- If no Response.encoding is specified and chardet is available,
Response.text will guess an encoding.

- Default to ISO-8859-1 (Western) encoding for “text” subtypes.

- Removal of decode\_unicode. ( _Backwards Incompatible_)

- New multiple-hooks system.

- New Response.register\_hook for registering hooks within the
pipeline.

- Response.url is now Unicode.

- session argument for Session classes.

## Description

### Impact

Lodash versions 4.0.0 through 4.17.22 are vulnerable to prototype pollution in the `_.unset` and `_.omit` functions. An attacker can pass crafted paths which cause Lodash to delete methods from global prototypes.

The issue permits deletion of properties but does not allow overwriting their original behavior.

### Patches

This issue is patched on 4.17.23

nvd.description: An issue was discovered in the node-serialize package 0.0.4 for Node.js. Untrusted data passed into the unserialize() function can be exploited to achieve arbitrary code execution by passing a JavaScript Object with an Immediately Invoked Function Expression (IIFE).

nvd.description: Requests is a HTTP library. Since Requests 2.3.0, Requests has been leaking Proxy-Authorization headers to destination servers when redirected to an HTTPS endpoint. This is a product of how we use `rebuild_proxies` to reattach the `Proxy-Authorization` header to requests. For HTTP connections sent through the tunnel, the proxy will identify the header in the request itself and remove it prior to forwarding to the destination server. However when sent over HTTPS, the `Proxy-Authorization` header must be sent in the CONNECT request as the proxy has no visibility into the tunneled request. This results in Requests forwarding proxy credentials to the destination server unintentionally, allowing a malicious actor to potentially exfiltrate sensitive information. This issue has been patched in version 2.31.0.

github_issues.title: [security][deps] Upgrade gunicorn (CVE-2024-1135) and requests (CVE-2023-32681); add Dependabot + pip-audit
github_issues.body:
**Lens:** Backend + DevOps audit · **Severity: Medium-High**

- `requirements.txt:7` pins `gunicorn==19.9.0` (2018) — the production WSGI server (`Procfile`, `Dockerfile.prod`) — which predates CVE-2024-1135 (HTTP request smuggling via malformed Transfer-Encoding; fixed in 22.0).
- `requirements.txt:11` pins `requests==2.25.1`, predating CVE-2023-32681 (proxy credential leak on redirect; fixed 2.31).
- `algoliasearch==2.6.1`, `dj-database-url==0.5.0` are years stale. Django 4.2.x and psycopg2 are fine.
- No `.github/dependabot.yml`, no CodeQL, no `pip-audit`/`yarn audit` in CI.

**Fix:** Bump gunicorn ≥23 and requests ≥2.32; add `dependabot.yml` covering pip + npm + github-actions; add a `pip-audit` CI step.

**Rough thoughts:** Gunicorn behind a proxy/tunnel is precisely the topology where request smuggling matters. Dependabot on a personal project is set-and-forget insurance.

Lodash versions 4.0.0 through 4.17.22 are vulnerable to prototype pollution in the `_.unset` and `_.omit` functions. An attacker can pass crafted paths which cause Lodash to delete methods from global prototypes.

The issue permits deletion of properties but does not allow overwriting their original behavior.

The Pallets team is pleased to release [Flask](https://flask.palletsprojects.com/) 1.0.

The Flask framework has been stable for a long time. A little more than 8 years after
the first commit, the version number finally reflects that. 1.0 comes with a significant
number of changes representing over a year of work.

- Dropped support for Python 2.6 and 3.3.
- The CLI is more flexible. `FLASK_APP` can point to an app factory, optionally with
  arguments. It understands import names in more cases where filenames were previously
  used. It automatically detects common filenames, app names, and factory
  names. `FLASK_ENV` describes the environment the app is running in,
  like `development`, and replaces `FLASK_DEBUG` in most
  cases. [See the docs to learn more.](https://flask.palletsprojects.com/page/cli/)
- If python-dotenv is installed, the `flask` CLI will load environment variables
  from `.flaskenv` and `.env` files rather than having to export them in each new
  terminal.
- The development server is multi-threaded by default to handle concurrent requests
  during development.
- `flask.ext`, which was previously deprecated, is completely removed. Import
  extensions by their actual package names.
- Accessing missing keys from `request.form` shows a more helpful error message in
  debug mode, addressing a very common source of confusion for developers.
- Error handlers are looked up by code then exception class, on the blueprint then
  application. This gives more predictable control over handlers, including being able
  to handle `HTTPException`.
- The behavior of `app.logger` has been greatly simplified and should be much easier
  to customize. The logger is always named `flask.app`, it only adds a handler if none
  are registered, and it never removes existing
  handlers. [See the docs to learn more.](https://flask.palletsprojects.com/page/logging/)
- The `test_client` gained a `json` argument for posting JSON data, and
  the `Response` object gained a `get_json` method to decode the data as JSON in
  tests.
- A new `test_cli_runner` is added for testing an app's CLI commands.
- Many documentation sections have been rewritten to improve clarity and relevance. This
  is an ongoing effort.
- The [tutorial](https://flask.palletsprojects.com/page/tutorial/) and
  corresponding [example](https://github.com/pallets/flask/tree/1.0/examples/tutorial)
  have been rewritten. They use a structured layout and go into more detail about each
  aspect in order to help new users avoid common issues and become comfortable with
  Flask.

There are many more changes throughout the
framework. [Read the full changelog](https://flask.palletsprojects.com/page/changes/) to
understand what changes may affect your code when upgrading.

## JSON Security Fix [¶](https://www.palletsprojects.com/blog/flask-1-0-released/\#json-security-fix)

Flask previously decoded incoming JSON bytes using the content type of the request.
Although JSON should only be encoded as UTF-8, Flask was more lenient. However, Python
includes non-text related encodings that could result in unexpected memory use by a
request.

Flask will now detect the encoding of incoming JSON data as one of the supported UTF
encodings, and will not allow arbitrary encodings from the request.

## Install or Upgrade [¶](https://www.palletsprojects.com/blog/flask-1-0-released/\#install-or-upgrade)

Install from [PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/Flask/) with pip:

```
pip install -U Flask
```

## Get Involved [¶](https://www.palletsprojects.com/blog/flask-1-0-released/\#get-involved)

Flask and the Pallets team depends on you, the community. Whether you report issues,
write documentation, create patches, or answer questions, we appreciate all the help you
provide. Check out
the [contributing guide](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.rst) to
get started.

## Donate [¶](https://www.palletsprojects.com/blog/flask-1-0-released/\#donate)

The Pallets organization has joined the Python Software Foundation's Fiscal Sponsorship
program. We now accept donations through the PSF in order to support our efforts to
maintain the projects and grow the community. [Click here to donate.](https://www.palletsprojects.com/blog/donate)

## Siemens Security Advisory by Siemens ProductCERT

## Vulnerability CVE-2021-23839

OpenSSL 1.0.2 supports SSLv2. If a client attempts to negotiate SSLv2 with a server that is configured to support both SSLv2 and more recent SSL and TLS versions then a check is made for a version rollback attack when unpadding an RSA signature. Clients that support SSL or TLS versions greater than SSLv2 are supposed to use a special form of padding. A server that supports greater than SSLv2 is supposed to reject connection attempts from a client where this special form of padding is present, because this indicates that a version rollback has occurred (i.e. both client and server support greater than SSLv2, and yet this is the version that is being requested). The implementation of this padding check inverted the logic so that the connection attempt is accepted if the padding is present, and rejected if it is absent. This means that such as server will accept a connection if a version rollback attack has occurred. Further the server will erroneously reject a connection if a normal SSLv2 connection attempt is made. Only OpenSSL 1.0.2 servers from version 1.0.2s to 1.0.2x are affected by this issue. In order to be vulnerable a 1.0.2 server must: 1) have configured SSLv2 support at compile time (this is off by default), 2) have configured SSLv2 support at runtime (this is off by default), 3) have configured SSLv2 ciphersuites (these are not in the default ciphersuite list) OpenSSL 1.1.1 does not have SSLv2 support and therefore is not vulnerable to this issue. The underlying error is in the implementation of the RSA\_padding\_check\_SSLv23() function. This also affects the RSA\_SSLV23\_PADDING padding mode used by various other functions. Although

1.1.1 does not support SSLv2 the RSA\_padding\_check\_SSLv23() function still exists, as does the RSA\_SSLV23\_PADDING padding mode. Applications that directly call that function or use that padding mode will encounter this issue. However since there is no support for the SSLv2 protocol in 1.1.1 this is considered a bug and not a security issue in that version. OpenSSL 1.0.2 is out of support and no longer receiving public updates. Premium support customers of OpenSSL 1.0.2 should upgrade to
1.0.2y. Other users should upgrade to 1.1.1j. Fixed in OpenSSL 1.0.2y (Affected 1.0.2s-1.0.2x). CVSS v3.1 Base Score 3.7 CVSS VectorCVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:L/A:N/E:P/RL:O/RC:C CWE CWE-326: Inadequate Encryption Strength

## Vulnerability CVE-2021-23841

The OpenSSL public API function X509\_issuer\_and\_serial\_hash() attempts to create a unique hash value based on the issuer and serial number data contained within an X509 certificate. However it fails to correctly handle any errors that may occur while parsing the issuer field (which might occur if the issuer field is maliciously constructed). This may subsequently result in a NULL pointer deref and a crash leading to a potential denial of service attack. The function X509\_issuer\_and\_serial\_hash() is never directly called by OpenSSL itself so applications are only vulnerable if they use this function directly and they use it on certificates that may have been obtained from untrusted sources. OpenSSL versions 1.1.1i and below are affected by this issue. Users of these versions should upgrade to OpenSSL 1.1.1j. OpenSSL versions 1.0.2x and below are affected by this issue. However OpenSSL

1.0.2 is out of support and no longer receiving public updates. Premium support customers of OpenSSL 1.0.2 should upgrade to 1.0.2y. Other users should upgrade to 1.1.1j. Fixed in OpenSSL
1.1.1j (Affected 1.1.1-1.1.1i). Fixed in OpenSSL 1.0.2y (Affected 1.0.2-1.0.2x). CVSS v3.1 Base Score 5.9 CVSS VectorCVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H/E:P/RL:O/RC:C CWE CWE-311: Missing Encryption of Sensitive Data

## PRODUCT DESCRIPTION

SINEC INS (Infrastructure Network Services) is a web-based application that combines various network services in one tool. This simplifies installation and administration of all network services relevant for industrial networks.

## VULNERABILITY CLASSIFICATION

The vulnerability classification has been performed by using the CVSS scoring system in version 3.1 (CVSS v3.1) ( [https://www.first.org/cvss/](https://www.first.org/cvss/)). The CVSS environmental score is specific to the customer’s environment and will impact the overall CVSS score. The environmental score should therefore be individually defined by the customer to accomplish final scoring.

An additional classification has been performed using the CWE classification, a community-developed list of common software security weaknesses. This serves as a common language and as a baseline for weakness identification, mitigation, and prevention efforts. A detailed list of CWE classes can be found at: [https://cwe.mitre.org/](https://cwe.mitre.org/).

## Vulnerability CVE-2021-4160

There is a carry propagation bug in the MIPS32 and MIPS64 squaring procedure. Many EC algorithms are affected, including some of the TLS 1.3 default curves. Impact was not analyzed in detail, because the pre-requisites for attack are considered unlikely and include reusing private keys. Analysis suggests that attacks against RSA and DSA as a result of this defect would be very difficult to perform and are not believed likely. Attacks against DH are considered just feasible (although very difficult) because most of the work necessary to deduce information about a private key may be performed offline. The amount of resources required for such an attack would be significant. However, for an attack on TLS to be meaningful, the server would have to share the DH private key among multiple clients, which is no longer an option since CVE-2016-0701. This issue affects OpenSSL versions

1.0.2, 1.1.1 and 3.0.0. It was addressed in the releases of 1.1.1m and 3.0.1 on the 15th of December
2021\. For the 1.0.2 release it is addressed in git commit 6fc1aaaf3 that is available to premium support customers only. It will be made available in 1.0.2zc when it is released. The issue only affects OpenSSL on MIPS platforms. Fixed in OpenSSL 3.0.1 (Affected 3.0.0). Fixed in OpenSSL 1.1.1m (Affected 1.1.1-1.1.1l). Fixed in OpenSSL 1.0.2zc-dev (Affected 1.0.2-1.0.2zb). ## Siemens Security Advisory by Siemens ProductCERT

## Vulnerability CVE-2021-23839

OpenSSL 1.0.2 supports SSLv2. If a client attempts to negotiate SSLv2 with a server that is configured to support both SSLv2 and more recent SSL and TLS versions then a check is made for a version rollback attack when unpadding an RSA signature. Clients that support SSL or TLS versions greater than SSLv2 are supposed to use a special form of padding. A server that supports greater than SSLv2 is supposed to reject connection attempts from a client where this special form of padding is present, because this indicates that a version rollback has occurred (i.e. both client and server support greater than SSLv2, and yet this is the version that is being requested). The implementation of this padding check inverted the logic so that the connection attempt is accepted if the padding is present, and rejected if it is absent. This means that such as server will accept a connection if a version rollback attack has occurred. Further the server will erroneously reject a connection if a normal SSLv2 connection attempt is made. Only OpenSSL 1.0.2 servers from version 1.0.2s to 1.0.2x are affected by this issue. In order to be vulnerable a 1.0.2 server must: 1) have configured SSLv2 support at compile time (this is off by default), 2) have configured SSLv2 support at runtime (this is off by default), 3) have configured SSLv2 ciphersuites (these are not in the default ciphersuite list) OpenSSL 1.1.1 does not have SSLv2 support and therefore is not vulnerable to this issue. The underlying error is in the implementation of the RSA\_padding\_check\_SSLv23() function. This also affects the RSA\_SSLV23\_PADDING padding mode used by various other functions. Although

1.1.1 does not support SSLv2 the RSA\_padding\_check\_SSLv23() function still exists, as does the RSA\_SSLV23\_PADDING padding mode. Applications that directly call that function or use that padding mode will encounter this issue. However since there is no support for the SSLv2 protocol in 1.1.1 this is considered a bug and not a security issue in that version. OpenSSL 1.0.2 is out of support and no longer receiving public updates. Premium support customers of OpenSSL 1.0.2 should upgrade to
1.0.2y. Other users should upgrade to 1.1.1j. Fixed in OpenSSL 1.0.2y (Affected 1.0.2s-1.0.2x). CVSS v3.1 Base Score 3.7 CVSS VectorCVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:L/A:N/E:P/RL:O/RC:C CWE CWE-326: Inadequate Encryption Strength

## Vulnerability CVE-2021-23841

The OpenSSL public API function X509\_issuer\_and\_serial\_hash() attempts to create a unique hash value based on the issuer and serial number data contained within an X509 certificate. However it fails to correctly handle any errors that may occur while parsing the issuer field (which might occur if the issuer field is maliciously constructed). This may subsequently result in a NULL pointer deref and a crash leading to a potential denial of service attack. The function X509\_issuer\_and\_serial\_hash() is never directly called by OpenSSL itself so applications are only vulnerable if they use this function directly and they use it on certificates that may have been obtained from untrusted sources. OpenSSL versions 1.1.1i and below are affected by this issue. Users of these versions should upgrade to OpenSSL 1.1.1j. OpenSSL versions 1.0.2x and below are affected by this issue. However OpenSSL

1.0.2 is out of support and no longer receiving public updates. Premium support customers of OpenSSL 1.0.2 should upgrade to 1.0.2y. Other users should upgrade to 1.1.1j. Fixed in OpenSSL
1.1.1j (Affected 1.1.1-1.1.1i). Fixed in OpenSSL 1.0.2y (Affected 1.0.2-1.0.2x). CVSS v3.1 Base Score 5.9 CVSS VectorCVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H/E:P/RL:O/RC:C CWE CWE-311: Missing Encryption of Sensitive Data

nvd.description:
Flask is a lightweight WSGI web application framework. When all of the following conditions are met, a response containing data intended for one client may be cached and subsequently sent by the proxy to other clients. If the proxy also caches `Set-Cookie` headers, it may send one client's `session` cookie to other clients. The severity depends on the application's use of the session and the proxy's behavior regarding cookies. The risk depends on all these conditions being met.

1. The application must be hosted behind a caching proxy that does not strip cookies or ignore responses with cookies.
2. The application sets `session.permanent = True`
3. The application does not access or modify the session at any point during a request.
4. `SESSION_REFRESH_EACH_REQUEST` enabled (the default).
5. The application does not set a `Cache-Control` header to indicate that a page is private or should not be cached.

This happens because vulnerable versions of Flask only set the `Vary: Cookie` header when the session is accessed or modified, not when it is refreshed (re-sent to update the expiration) without being accessed or modified. This issue has been fixed in versions 2.3.2 and 2.2.5.

nvd.description: Express.js minimalist web framework for node. Versions of Express.js prior to 4.19.0 and all pre-release alpha and beta versions of 5.0 are affected by an open redirect vulnerability using malformed URLs. When a user of Express performs a redirect using a user-provided URL Express performs an encode [using `encodeurl`](https://github.com/pillarjs/encodeurl) on the contents before passing it to the `location` header. This can cause malformed URLs to be evaluated in unexpected ways by common redirect allow list implementations in Express applications, leading to an Open Redirect via bypass of a properly implemented allow list. The main method impacted is `res.location()` but this is also called from within `res.redirect()`. The vulnerability is fixed in 4.19.2 and 5.0.0-beta.3.

rag_summaries.attack_vector: Attacker supplies a crafted string with many spaces between digits to lodash toNumber, trim, or trimEnd, triggering catastrophic backtracking and denial of service.
rag_summaries.mitigation: Upgrade lodash to version 4.17.21 or later.

analysis.description: Maliciously crafted input such as '1' followed by thousands of spaces and then '1' causes inefficient regular expression matching in toNumber, trim, and trimEnd, consuming excessive CPU.
conditions: Application uses lodash prior to 4.17.21
User-controlled input reaches lodash toNumber, trim, or trimEnd

rag_summaries.summary: Lodash before 4.17.21 is vulnerable to ReDoS through toNumber, trim, and trimEnd when processing crafted input, causing denial of service.

rag_summaries.attack_vector: Command Injection via the lodash _.template function. Attacker-controlled input passed through the template variable option or options.imports key names reaches a Function() constructor sink and is executed as JavaScript.
rag_summaries.mitigation: Upgrade lodash to 4.17.21 or later and avoid passing untrusted input to _.template options.

analysis.description: Lodash versions prior to 4.17.21 are vulnerable to Command Injection via the template function. The fix for CVE-2021-23337 added validation for the variable option but not for options.imports key names; both paths flow into the same Function() constructor sink.
conditions: lodash version is prior to 4.17.21
Application passes attacker-controlled input to _.template options, such as variable or options.imports key names
The untrusted input reaches the Function() constructor sink

rag_summaries.summary: Command injection in lodash _.template occurs when attacker-controlled template options reach the Function() constructor, enabling arbitrary code execution in affected versions before 4.17.21.

rag_summaries.attack_vector: An attacker passes crafted property paths to _.unset or _.omit, causing Lodash to delete properties/methods from global prototypes.
rag_summaries.mitigation: Upgrade lodash to version 4.17.23 or later.

analysis.description: Crafted paths supplied to _.unset and _.omit cause deletion of methods from global prototypes. The issue permits property deletion but not overwriting original behavior.
conditions: Application uses lodash _.unset or _.omit with attacker-influenced path input
Affected version is >=4.0.0 and <=4.17.22

rag_summaries.summary: Lodash 4.0.0 through 4.17.22 is vulnerable to prototype pollution via crafted paths to _.unset and _.omit, allowing deletion of global prototype methods; patched in 4.17.23.

rag_summaries.attack_vector: Prototype pollution via lodash _.zipObjectDeep: an attacker supplies a crafted key path such as ['__proto__.z'] with a value, causing Object.prototype pollution. This can crash the server (denial of service) and may lead to remote code execution in some cases.
rag_summaries.mitigation: Upgrade lodash to version 4.17.20 or later. Avoid passing untrusted/unsanitized key paths to _.zipObjectDeep and block dangerous keys such as __proto__, constructor, and prototype.

analysis.description: Attacker passes a crafted key path containing '__proto__.z' to _.zipObjectDeep, which writes a property directly to Object.prototype and makes it visible on all objects, enabling denial of service and potentially remote code execution.
conditions: Application calls lodash _.zipObjectDeep with attacker-controlled key paths
lodash version is before 4.17.20
Input is not sanitized or filtered for dangerous keys like __proto__

rag_summaries.summary: lodash before 4.17.20 allows prototype pollution through _.zipObjectDeep with attacker-controlled keys such as '__proto__.z', causing Object.prototype injection; upgrade to 4.17.20 or sanitize input.

rag_summaries.attack_vector: An attacker supplies malicious input that reaches Lodash's template function. The vulnerable versions pass untrusted template options into a Function() constructor sink, enabling command injection/code execution.
rag_summaries.mitigation: Upgrade lodash to 4.17.21 or later.

analysis.description: Lodash versions prior to 4.17.21 are vulnerable to Command Injection via the template function. The template function uses a Function() constructor sink without properly neutralizing attacker-controlled template options, allowing injected code to execute.
conditions: Application uses lodash version prior to 4.17.21
Untrusted input reaches the _.template function or its template options
Attacker controls template options such as variable or options.imports key names

rag_summaries.summary: Lodash before 4.17.21 is exploitable through the template function, enabling command injection/code execution when untrusted template options reach the Function() constructor sink.

rag_summaries.attack_vector: An attacker passes crafted paths to _.unset or _.omit, causing deletion of methods from global prototypes.
rag_summaries.mitigation: Upgrade lodash to 4.17.23 or later.

analysis.description: Crafted paths supplied to _.unset or _.omit delete properties from global prototypes. The issue permits deletion of properties but does not allow overwriting their original behavior.
conditions: Lodash version >=4.0.0 and <=4.17.22
Attacker-controlled path input reaches _.unset or _.omit

rag_summaries.summary: Prototype pollution in lodash _.unset and _.omit allows an attacker to delete global prototype methods via crafted paths; fixed in 4.17.23.

rag_summaries.attack_vector: Passing untrusted user input to response.redirect() in Express < 4.20.0 can execute untrusted code via a crafted javascript: URL rendered in the redirect response body.
rag_summaries.mitigation: Upgrade to express 4.20.0 or 5.0.0. If upgrading is not possible, validate untrusted inputs against an explicit allowlist before passing to response.redirect().

analysis.description: An attacker controls the input to response.redirect(); Express renders the attacker-influenced redirect URL in an HTML anchor. A malicious javascript: URL can execute code if the user clicks the link before the browser completes the redirect.
conditions: The attacker controls input passed to response.redirect()
Express does not redirect before the template appears
The browser does not complete redirection before the user clicks the link
The user clicks the attacker-controlled link in the template

rag_summaries.summary: CVE-2024-43796 is an XSS vulnerability in Express < 4.20.0 where untrusted input passed to response.redirect() can execute code through a malicious javascript: link when a user clicks the rendered redirect URL.

rag_summaries.attack_vector: An attacker supplies a malformed URL to an Express application endpoint that passes user input to res.location() or res.redirect(). Express encodes the URL with encodeurl before setting the Location header, which can change how the URL is interpreted and bypass allow-list checks, leading to an open redirect.
rag_summaries.mitigation: Upgrade Express to 4.19.2 or 5.0.0-beta.3, which validate that URL parsing after encoding does not alter the host.

analysis.description: Malformed user-supplied URLs passed to redirect or location are encoded before being set in the Location header. The encoding can cause common allow-list implementations to see a safe host while browsers interpret a different host, bypassing the allow list.
conditions: Express version is prior to 4.19.0 or an affected 5.0 alpha/beta release
Application passes user-controlled URL to res.location() or res.redirect()
Application relies on a URL allow-list check that is bypassed by the encoded malformed URL

rag_summaries.summary: CVE-2024-29041 is a medium-severity open redirect in Express caused by encoding malformed user-supplied URLs before setting the Location header, allowing allow-list bypass; fixed in 4.19.2 and 5.0.0-beta.3.

rag_summaries.attack_vector: An attacker supplies untrusted data to unserialize() containing a string property prefixed with _$$ND_FUNC$$_ whose value is an IIFE. During deserialization, the string is passed to eval and executed, leading to remote code execution.
rag_summaries.mitigation: Do not pass untrusted data to node-serialize unserialize(); remove or replace the library with a safe deserialization approach that does not use eval.

analysis.description: unserialize() parses JSON and calls eval on any string value beginning with _$$ND_FUNC$$_. A crafted payload ending with () forms an IIFE that executes attacker-controlled JavaScript when eval is reached.
conditions: Untrusted input reaches serialize.unserialize()
Payload contains a string property starting with _$$ND_FUNC$$_
The string contains an IIFE such as function(){...}() to trigger execution during eval

rag_summaries.summary: node-serialize 0.0.4 unserialize() evaluates _$$ND_FUNC$$_-prefixed strings via eval, allowing remote code execution when untrusted input carries an IIFE payload.

rag_summaries.attack_vector: An attacker sends crafted JSON data using an arbitrary non-UTF encoding or content type to a Flask endpoint that decodes incoming JSON, causing unexpected memory usage.
rag_summaries.mitigation: Upgrade Flask to version 1.0 or later, which detects and restricts incoming JSON encodings to supported UTF encodings.

analysis.description: Flask before 1.0 decoded incoming JSON bytes based on the request content type and allowed arbitrary encodings. Crafted non-UTF encoded JSON data can trigger unexpected memory usage.
conditions: Flask version before 1.0
Application decodes incoming JSON request data
Attacker supplies JSON data with an unsupported non-UTF encoding

rag_summaries.summary: Flask before 1.0 is vulnerable to denial of service through crafted non-UTF encoded JSON data that causes unexpected memory usage during request decoding.

rag_summaries.attack_vector: In Flask 3.1.2 and below, key-only session access operations such as the Python `in` and `len` operators do not mark the session as accessed, so Flask fails to set the `Vary: Cookie` header. When deployed behind a caching proxy that caches responses containing cookies and without a private/no-cache Cache-Control header, a response containing user-specific session data can be cached and served to other users.
rag_summaries.mitigation: Upgrade Flask to version 3.1.3 or later, which marks the session as accessed for key-only operations such as `in` and `len` and ensures the `Vary: Cookie` header is set.

analysis.type: Use of Cache Containing Sensitive Information
analysis.description: Session access through key-only operations like `in` and `len` was not tracked as session access, so Flask did not add `Vary: Cookie`. A shared cache could then store a user-specific response and later serve it to a different user.
conditions: Application is hosted behind a caching proxy that does not ignore responses with cookies
No Cache-Control header is set to mark pages as private or non-cacheable
The session is accessed only via keys without reading values or mutating the session, e.g. using the Python `in` or `len` operators
Flask version is 3.1.2 or below

rag_summaries.summary: Flask <=3.1.2 may omit the `Vary: Cookie` header when session keys are checked with `in`/`len`, allowing a caching proxy to serve sensitive user-specific responses to other users; fixed in 3.1.3.

rag_summaries.attack_vector: A Flask application hosted behind a caching proxy may omit the `Vary: Cookie` header when a permanent session is refreshed without being accessed or modified. The proxy can then cache a response or `Set-Cookie` session cookie intended for one client and serve it to another client.
rag_summaries.mitigation: Upgrade Flask to 2.3.2 or 2.2.5. As a workaround, set a `Cache-Control` header such as `private` or `no-cache` to prevent caching.

analysis.description: When the session is refreshed but not accessed or modified, vulnerable Flask versions do not add `Vary: Cookie`, so an upstream caching proxy may cache and replay responses or session cookies across clients.
conditions: The application is hosted behind a caching proxy that does not strip cookies or ignore responses with cookies.
The application sets `session.permanent = True`.
The application does not access or modify the session during the request.
`SESSION_REFRESH_EACH_REQUEST` is enabled, which is the default.
The application does not set a `Cache-Control` header indicating the page is private or should not be cached.

rag_summaries.summary: CVE-2023-30861 allows cached responses or `Set-Cookie` session cookies to be served to unintended clients when Flask omits `Vary: Cookie` during session refresh; exploitable only behind a permissive caching proxy with specific session configuration.

rag_summaries.attack_vector: A remote attacker sends a crafted malformed JSON payload to an endpoint that parses JSON via Flask's request.get_json(), causing an unhandled JSON decode exception and crashing the application.
rag_summaries.mitigation: Upgrade Flask to version 0.12.3 or later.

analysis.description: Malformed JSON input triggers an unhandled exception in Flask's JSON parsing, leading to application crash.
conditions: Application runs Flask 0.12.2 or earlier
An endpoint invokes Flask JSON parsing such as request.get_json()
Attacker can send an HTTP request with a JSON content type and malformed JSON body

rag_summaries.summary: Flask 0.12.2 is remotely exploitable to cause denial of service through malformed JSON request parsing; upgrade to 0.12.3 or later mitigates this.

rag_summaries.attack_vector: An attacker supplies a user-controlled filename containing CRLF sequences (%0d%0a) to an endpoint that passes it to Flask's send_file function, enabling injection of arbitrary HTTP response headers.
rag_summaries.mitigation: Upgrade Flask to 1.0.3 or later, or sanitize and reject CRLF characters in filenames passed to send_file.

analysis.description: Flask send_file fails to sanitize CRLF sequences in the attachment filename, allowing arbitrary response headers and possible reflected XSS.
conditions: Application uses Flask before 1.0.3
User-controlled filename is passed to send_file
Filename contains CRLF sequences

rag_summaries.summary: Flask 0.12.2 is vulnerable to HTTP header injection through unsanitized user-controlled filenames in send_file, enabling arbitrary response headers and potential XSS.

rag_summaries.attack_vector: An attacker uses a shared HTTP cache to receive a cached response containing a refreshed session cookie because Flask does not set the Vary: Cookie header, enabling session cookie disclosure.
rag_summaries.mitigation: Upgrade Flask to version 2.2.5 or 2.3.2 or later, which adds the Vary: Cookie header to session-refreshing responses.

analysis.description: A response that refreshes a session cookie can be cached and later served to a different user because the Vary: Cookie header is missing.
conditions: An intermediate or shared HTTP cache is used
The application response refreshes or contains a session cookie
The cached response is requested by another user

rag_summaries.summary: CVE-2023-30861 in Flask 0.12.2 allows cached session-cookie responses to be served to other users due to missing Vary: Cookie, potentially disclosing session cookies.

rag_summaries.mitigation: None

rag_summaries.attack_vector: A maliciously crafted URL such as http://victim.com:@evil.com/ is parsed incorrectly, causing requests to send .netrc credentials configured for victim.com to the attacker-controlled host evil.com.
rag_summaries.mitigation: Upgrade requests to 2.32.4 or later. For older versions, disable .netrc credential lookup by setting trust_env=False on the requests.Session.

analysis.description: Due to incorrect parsing of the URL netloc component, .netrc credentials for one host are sent to a different attacker-controlled host when a crafted URL is requested.
conditions: requests version < 2.32.4
A .netrc file contains credentials for the target host
trust_env is enabled (default), allowing .netrc lookup
An attacker can influence or supply a crafted URL such as http://victim.com:@evil.com/

rag_summaries.summary: CVE-2024-47081 allows credential leakage from .netrc to attacker-controlled hosts via maliciously crafted URLs in vulnerable requests versions.

rag_summaries.attack_vector: The vulnerability is exploited when a `requests.Session` makes its first request to a given host with `verify=False` to disable TLS certificate verification. Subsequent requests to the same host will continue to ignore certificate verification even if `verify=True` is explicitly set, due to connection pooling reusing the same unverified TLS connection.
rag_summaries.mitigation: Upgrade `requests` to version 2.32.0 or later. Alternatively, avoid setting `verify=False` for the first request to a host when using a Session, or call `close()` on the Session to clear the connection pool after using `verify=False`.

analysis.description: If the first request to a host using a `requests.Session` disables TLS verification with `verify=False`, all subsequent requests to that host will also bypass certificate validation, enabling man-in-the-middle attacks on those later requests.
conditions: The application uses `requests.Session`
The first request to a specific host is made with `verify=False`
Subsequent requests to the same host are made (with or without `verify=True`)

rag_summaries.summary: A session's connection pool reuses TLS settings from the first request; if `verify=False` is used initially, all later requests to the same host skip certificate validation, allowing MITM attacks.

rag_summaries.attack_vector: A local attacker with write access to the system temporary directory pre-creates a malicious file at the predictable path used by requests.utils.extract_zipped_paths(); when extracting a zip member with the same basename, the existing file is reused without validation and loaded in place of the legitimate one.
rag_summaries.mitigation: Upgrade requests to 2.33.0 or later, where extract_zipped_paths() extracts to a non-deterministic location. If upgrading is not possible, set TMPDIR to a directory with restricted write access.

analysis.description: extract_zipped_paths() joins the zip member basename to the system temporary directory and reuses an existing file without validation. A local attacker who can write to the temp directory plants a malicious file at that path, which is then loaded instead of the legitimate extracted file.
conditions: Application directly calls requests.utils.extract_zipped_paths()
Local attacker has write access to the system temporary directory
The target file already exists and is reused without validation

rag_summaries.summary: CVE-2026-25645 is a local insecure temporary file vulnerability in requests' extract_zipped_paths() utility; exploitation requires direct use of that function and a local attacker able to pre-create a malicious file in the predictable temp path.

rag_summaries.attack_vector: When a proxy URL contains credentials and a request is redirected to an HTTPS endpoint, the Proxy-Authorization header is reattached and sent through the tunnel to the destination server, leaking proxy credentials.
rag_summaries.mitigation: Upgrade requests to version 2.31.0 or later and rotate any exposed proxy credentials.

analysis.description: The rebuild_proxies function reattaches the Proxy-Authorization header to requests after redirects. For HTTPS destinations, this header is tunneled to the target server instead of being consumed by the proxy, allowing a malicious destination to capture proxy credentials.
conditions: Requests version between 2.3.0 and 2.30.0
Proxy is configured with username and password in the proxy URL
Request follows a redirect to an HTTPS endpoint

rag_summaries.summary: Versions 2.3.0 through 2.30.0 of requests leak Proxy-Authorization headers to destination HTTPS servers after redirects when proxy credentials are embedded in the proxy URL. Upgrading to 2.31.0+ and rotating exposed credentials mitigates the issue.

rag_summaries.attack_vector: The Requests library sends an HTTP Authorization header to an http URI upon receiving a same-hostname https-to-http redirect, allowing network sniffers to capture credentials.
rag_summaries.mitigation: Upgrade to requests version 2.20.0 or later. Alternatively, avoid following redirects or ensure redirects do not downgrade to HTTP.

analysis.description: Exploitation occurs when an HTTPS request with an Authorization header is redirected to an HTTP URL on the same hostname; the library transmits the Authorization header to the insecure HTTP endpoint, enabling credential interception.
conditions: Application uses requests with an Authorization header
Request is made over HTTPS
Server responds with redirect to HTTP URL on same hostname
Requests library follows redirects (default behavior)

rag_summaries.summary: Requests <=2.19.0 leaks Authorization header credentials via HTTPS-to-HTTP redirects to the same host, enabling network sniffing.

rag_summaries.attack_vector: An attacker on the network intercepts an HTTP request containing the Authorization header after requests follows a same-hostname HTTPS-to-HTTP redirect, exposing credentials.
rag_summaries.mitigation: Upgrade requests to version 2.20.0 or later.

analysis.description: requests sends the HTTP Authorization header to a plaintext http:// URI when redirected from an HTTPS URL on the same host, exposing credentials to network sniffing.
conditions: Application uses requests with redirects enabled (default)
A same-hostname HTTPS-to-HTTP redirect occurs
The request includes an Authorization header

rag_summaries.summary: requests before 2.20.0 leaks Authorization credentials over plaintext HTTP on same-host HTTPS-to-HTTP redirects; network attackers can sniff them. Upgrade to 2.20.0+.

rag_summaries.attack_vector: When requests is configured with an HTTP(S) proxy using Proxy-Authorization credentials, a destination server can return a cross-origin redirect. The vulnerable library forwards the Proxy-Authorization header to the redirected host, leaking proxy credentials to an unintended destination.
rag_summaries.mitigation: Upgrade requests to 2.31.0 or later, which strips Proxy-Authorization headers on cross-origin redirects.

analysis.description: The attack is executed by causing a cross-origin redirect while requests is configured with proxy authentication; the Proxy-Authorization header is then transmitted to the redirected host instead of being stripped.
conditions: requests version < 2.31.0 is used
A proxy is configured with Proxy-Authorization credentials
The destination server returns a cross-origin redirect

rag_summaries.summary: requests before 2.31.0 leaks Proxy-Authorization headers to cross-origin redirect targets, exposing proxy credentials. Upgrade to 2.31.0 or later to remediate.

rag_summaries.attack_vector: An attacker-controlled HTTPS server responds with a redirect to an HTTP URL on the same host. The vulnerable requests client follows the redirect and forwards the Authorization header in cleartext over HTTP, enabling credential interception.
rag_summaries.mitigation: Upgrade requests to version 2.20.0 or later; do not send Authorization headers over plaintext HTTP redirects.

conditions: requests version < 2.20.0
Request contains an Authorization header
HTTPS response redirects to HTTP on the same host

rag_summaries.summary: requests 2.19.0 is vulnerable to Authorization header disclosure over cleartext HTTP during same-host HTTPS-to-HTTP redirects; upgrade to 2.20.0+.
